```{r setup, echo=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(ggplot2)
library(DT)

set.seed(303)
n_assets <- 4
n_portfolios <- 500

# Simulate multi-asset portfolio simulations for Efficient Frontier
returns_mat <- matrix(rnorm(n_portfolios * n_assets, mean = 0.0005, sd = 0.02), ncol = n_assets)
port_returns <- apply(returns_mat, 1, sum) * 252
port_volatility <- apply(returns_mat, 1, sd) * sqrt(252)
sharpe_ratio <- port_returns / port_volatility

efficient_df <- data.frame(
  Return = round(port_returns, 4),
  Volatility = round(port_volatility, 4),
  Sharpe = round(sharpe_ratio, 4)
)

datatable(head(efficient_df, 10), options = list(dom = 't', pageLength = 5), rownames = FALSE, caption = "Table 1: Simulated Portfolio Allocations")

summary_opt <- data.frame(
  Metric = c("Simulated Portfolios", "Max Sharpe Ratio", "Peak Annual Return", "Minimum Volatility"),
  Value = c(
    n_portfolios, 
    round(max(sharpe_ratio), 2), 
    paste0(round(max(port_returns)*100, 2), "%"), 
    paste0(round(min(port_volatility)*100, 2), "%")
  )
)

datatable(summary_opt, options = list(dom = 't'), rownames = FALSE, caption = "Table 2: Modern Portfolio Theory Optimization Metrics")

ggplot(efficient_df, aes(x = Volatility, y = Return, color = Sharpe)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "#3498db", high = "#e74c3c") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  labs(
    title = "Efficient Frontier & Sharpe Ratio Distribution",
    subtitle = "Monte Carlo simulation of optimal asset weight allocations",
    x = "Annualized Volatility (Risk)",
    y = "Expected Annual Return",
    color = "Sharpe"
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")
